title: Mean Twelve, Median Fifteen
statement: Five different positive integers have mean $12$ and median $15$. What is the largest possible value of the largest of the five integers?
hints: The five integers add up to $60$. List them in increasing order: which one is fixed?
To make the largest one as big as possible, make each of the other three as small as the conditions allow.
solution: Write the integers as $p < q < 15 < s < t$. Their sum is $60$, so $t = 45 - p - q - s$, and $p \ge 1$, $q \ge 2$, $s \ge 16$ give $t \le 26$. The integers $1, 2, 15, 16, 26$ attain it, so the answer is $26$.
